Love of Christ
luhv uhv KRYST
doctrinal phrase
From love (Old English lufu) and Christ; the redeeming love of the Lord Jesus for His people.

Biblical Definition

The love of Christ is the redeeming love of the Lord Jesus for His people, a love that surpasses knowledge and constrains the believer’s whole life. It is an eternal love, set on His own before the foundation of the world; a free love, owing nothing to any worth or loveliness in its objects, who were yet sinners and enemies when He died for them; a particular love, by which the Good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep, and Christ loved the church and gave Himself for it; a sovereign and effectual love, which does not merely offer but secures the salvation of the beloved; and an unchanging love, from which neither death nor life nor any creature can separate those who are in Christ Jesus. The supreme proof and measure of this love is the cross: greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends, and Christ commended His love in that while we were yet sinners He died for us. The love of Christ is not bare sentiment but costly self-giving unto death, and it both saves and transforms—the love of Christ constraineth us, says Paul, so that those who are loved live no longer to themselves but to Him who died for them and rose again. The dictionary holds the love of Christ as the warm center of the gospel, an electing, redeeming, persevering love, the believer’s deepest security and strongest motive to holiness.

Webster 1828 Definition

The redeeming love of Christ for His people—eternal, free, particular, effectual, and unchanging—proved supremely at the cross and constraining the believer’s whole life.

LOVE OF CHRIST, the redeeming love of the Lord Jesus for His people.

An eternal love, set on His own before the foundation of the world.

A free love, owing nothing to worth in its objects, who were sinners and enemies.

A particular and effectual love: the Good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.

An unchanging love, from which no creature can separate the believer.

Key Scripture

Joh 15:13 — "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends."

Rom 5:8 — "But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us."

Eph 5:25 — "Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;"

Rom 8:39 — "Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."

Modern Corruption

Christ’s love is sentimentalized into a feeling that affirms all and saves none, severed from the cross and from holiness.

expand to see more

The reigning corruption is the sentimentalizing of Christ’s love into a tolerant affection that affirms everyone as they are, demands no repentance, and threatens no judgment. This empties the word of its biblical meaning. The love of Christ is costly, going all the way to the cross to bear the wrath His people deserved; it is holy, calling its objects out of sin into obedience; and it is particular and effectual, actually saving those on whom it is set, not a vague benevolence toward all that saves no one in particular.

A further corruption uses “the love of Christ” to overthrow His commands—as if love meant approving what He forbids. But Christ Himself said, “If ye love me, keep my commandments,” and His love for us never sets His holiness aside. The dictionary holds the love of Christ in its full biblical weight: an electing, redeeming, persevering love proved by the cross, which both secures the believer forever and constrains him to live no longer to himself but to the One who loved him and gave Himself for him.

Hebrew Roots

The doctrine sets forth Christ’s self-giving love—eternal in its source, the cross in its measure, holiness in its fruit.

expand to see more

Greek agapē — self-giving, sacrificial love; the love that goes to the cross.

Greek sunechō — to constrain, compel; “the love of Christ constraineth us.”

The cross is the supreme proof and measure of this love.

It is particular: Christ “loved the church, and gave himself for it.”

It is unchanging: nothing can separate the believer from it.

Usage

"The love of Christ is preached as eternal, particular, and effectual, proved at the cross."

"“The love of Christ constraineth us” is cited as the great motive to holy living."

"It is defended against sentimental misuse that severs love from holiness and judgment."
